transcript: I did not think rolling up to my neighborhood cathedral to see a Shakespeare was in the cards, but The Public works wonders with Public Works. This brief run of Pericles at the Cathedral of Saint John the Divine is a concert adaptation featuring a lovely score by Troy Anthony, some seriously head-turning performances by Broadway favorites like Denée Benton and Alex Newell, and an ensemble of a hundred New Yorkers across all ages and all five city boroughs. This is site-specific and community-driven theatre at its best, and although Pericles isn't a play I'd otherwise really be anticipating, this production was an utter delight. With these kinds of free Shakespeare productions, I'm always gonna be excited about them and how they contribute to the theatrical and cultural landscape of the city no matter what, but it's a huge bonus when the production itself is also a knockout. And this one checked all the boxes — great music, a great cast, raw humor and emotion, and a clear directorial vision that works for the format of the production and the play itself. If I'm nitpicking, I guess I’s observe how the space was clearly not built for a theater production. It's rather narrow and deep, making sightlines kinda difficult, but there are monitors flanking the audience on either side to help with that. And really, the acoustics of the space, with it being a church, are more than sufficient to experience this gospel, musical theatre, and R&B-infused score in all its glory. With that, another program for my collection.
